In the context of a [[module (mathematics)|module]] ''M'' over a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'', the '''top''' of ''M'' is the largest [[semisimple module|semisimple]] [[quotient module]] of ''M'' if it exists. 

For finite-dimensional ''k''-algebras (''k'' a field) R, if rad(''M'') denotes the intersection of all proper [[maximal submodule]]s of ''M'' (the [[radical of a module|radical of the module]]), then the top of ''M'' is ''M''/rad(''M'').  In the case of local rings with maximal ideal ''P'', the top of ''M'' is ''M''/''PM''.  In general if ''R'' is a [[semilocal ring]] (=semi-artinian ring), that is, if ''R''/Rad(''R'') is an [[Artinian ring]], where Rad(''R'') is the [[Jacobson radical]] of ''R'', then ''M''/rad(''M'') is a semisimple module and is the top of ''M''.  This includes the cases of local rings and finite dimensional algebras over fields.
